To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown that the (γ,n)- and (n, γ) reactions are statistical in the region of the isomeric threshold, and that the excitation of the 190mIr and 196gAu high-spin states is due to direct γ-ray capture, and that the isomeric ratio for 198mAu is due to the competition between direct γ-ray capture and statistical γ-ray emission.
the isomeric yields in the (γ, n) reaction for 190Ir and for 196Au are consistent with statistical model calculations, but that the isomery yields for 198Au are not.
the isomeric ratios in the near-threshhold (γ,n) reactions for the 190Ir and the 196Au isotopes have been measured for the first time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the excitation functions and isomeric ratios in the near-through region.
the excitation of isomers by means of the (γ,γ') and (n, γ) reactions.
the production of high-spin isomeric states of Ir and Au isotopes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the (γ,n), (n,γ), and (d,p) reactions are statistical processes in the near-through region for all the nuclei studied, and the isomeric ratios are determined solely by the relative spins of the initial and final states.
the excitation of the high-spin isomers of 190Ir, 196Au, and 198Au in the (γ,pn) reactions at the threshold is of a statistical nature.
, in the near-through region, the (γ,n)-reactions show a statistical behavior.

the excitation of isomeric states is not enhanced in the (γ, n) reaction.
